apparatus.basis: Editor restores ϣ to complete ϣⲱⲛⲉ 'sickness'; the noun pairs naturally with ⲡⲙ̄ⲕⲁⲍ 'pain' in the bodily-affliction series.
Editor restores ⲍⲙ̄ (Lyc. = ϩⲙ̄) 'in'; standard preposition introducing 'his stripe' as locus of the sickness.
Editor restores ⲉ (relative ⲉⲧⲉⲣⲉ) + ⲓⲏⲥ (Jesus). The full title ⲓⲏⲥ ⲡⲡⲣⲓⲉ 'Jesus the Radiance' is standard Manichaean Christological epithet (cf. accumulated vocabulary).
Editor restores final ⲉ to complete ⲡⲡⲣⲓⲉ 'the Radiance.'
Editor restores ⲧ within ⲧⲛⲧⲁⲛⲧ 'be likened/compared.'
Editor restores ⲁ within ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'forth.'
Editor restores ⲛ as initial letter of ⲛ̄ⲧⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁ6 'from the Greatness.'
Editor restores ⲙⲡⲥⲁ to complete ⲡⲉⲧⲙⲡⲥⲁⲙⲡⲓⲧⲛⲉ 'that which is upon the lower side' (cf. accumulated vocabulary ⲡⲥⲁⲙⲡⲓⲧⲛⲉ); pair-partner with the just-stated ⲡⲥⲁⲛⲧⲡⲉ.
Editor restores ⲡ as initial letter of ⲡⲓⲧⲛ̄ 'lower.'
Editor restores ⲟⲩⲁⲛ to complete ⲉⲧⲟⲩⲁⲛⲍ 'which are manifest' — the standard Manichaean revelation-verb.
Editor restores ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ⲉⲛ; the negation ⲉⲛ is required to distinguish 'the hidden ones (which are NOT manifest)' from 'the ships of light (which ARE manifest)' in the immediately following ⲉⲓⲧⲉ-clause.
Editor restores ⲛⲍ ⲁ to complete ⲉⲧⲟⲩⲁⲛⲍ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'which are manifest forth.'
Editor restores ⲛ̄ⲧⲁϩ ⲡⲉ 'he it is' — the standard pivot phrase introducing the Christological identification (Jesus the Radiance is the one who reveals).
Editor restores ⲍⲁ ⲡ to complete the prepositional phrase 'concerning the glory.'
Editor restores ⲭⲏ to complete ⲯⲩⲭⲏ 'soul' — the standard 'living soul' (ⲯⲩⲭⲏ ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ) of Manichaean cosmology.
Editor restores ⲁ as initial letter of ⲁⲃⲁⲗ continuing on next line.
Editor restores ⲣ within ⲍⲁⲣⲁⲥ 'concerning her.'
Editor restores ⲁ as initial letter of ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ 'in/inward' (continues on next line).
Editor restores ⲙⲟⲥ to complete ⲟⲩⲁⲥⲡⲁⲥⲙⲟⲥ 'a kiss/greeting' (Greek ἀσπασμός; cf. accumulated vocabulary).
Editor restores ⲕ to complete ⲁϩⲧⲱⲕ 'he stood' (= ⲁϥⲧⲱⲕ from ⲧⲱⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗ 'stand fast'; cf. accumulated vocabulary).
Editor restores ⲡ as article of ⲡⲉⲣⲟ 'the river.'
Editor restores ⲁⲣ to complete ⲡⲁⲣⲙⲟⲩⲧⲉ 'Pharmouthi' (Coptic month corresponding roughly to April; the spring flood season of the Tigris). Standard Manichaean date-formula.
Editor restores final ⲉ to complete ⲍⲙ̄ⲙⲟⲩⲓⲉⲩⲉ 'the lions' (plural).

notes.decision: Translated 'wound.' ϣϭⲁ (with 6 = ϭ) functions here as the bodily affliction-noun paired with πληγή 'plague/blow' (cf. line 14-15 ⲡⲓϣ6ⲁ + ⲡⲡⲗⲏⲅⲏ). Possibly Lyc. reflex of a wound/injury root (cf. ϣⲱⲱⲧ 'cut'); semantic field confirmed by recurrence with ⲡⲗⲏⲅⲏ.

Translated 'shame.' Reading as ϣⲱⲱⲥ 'blame, contempt, shame' rather than ϣⲱⲥ 'shepherd' — the antithetical pair 'glory and shame' fits the rhetorical structure of the tongue speaking of all bodily aspects (praise/blame/pain). 'Shepherd of the body' would be incongruent here.
Translated 'his stripe.' ⲥⲁϣ = ⲉⲥⲏϣ 'blow, lash, stripe' (cf. accumulated vocabulary). The bodily wound on which sickness manifests.

Translated 'is compared to.' Standard Coptic ⲧⲛ̄ⲧⲱⲛ qualitative + ⲙⲙⲟ⸗ 'be likened to.' Per terminology principle, the correspondential meaning here is 'this' (the Manichaean teacher) IS in the same correspondential register as the proclaiming tongue — Jesus the Radiance is the cosmic counterpart who reveals what is hidden.

Translated 'concerning the manifestation forth.' ⲁⲧ-ϭⲓⲛ-ⲟⲩⲱⲛϩ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ = preposition 'unto/concerning' + action-noun 'the manifesting forth.' ⲡⲓϩⲧⲁⲩ ⲛⲓⲱⲧ = 'these four fathers' — the four cosmic Fathers whose hidden/revealing operation is the topic of the closing kephalaion.

Translated 'Teaching.' Reading ⲧⲍⲃⲥⲱ as Lycopolitan variant of ⲧⲥⲃⲱ 'the teaching' with epenthetic ⲍ-onset (cf. accumulated vocabulary entry on ⲧϣⲁⲙⲧⲉ ⲛ̄ⲍⲃⲥⲱ ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ̄ rendered 'three Living Teachings' despite literal ϩⲃⲥⲱ 'garment' — the technical use is 'teaching/lesson'). Per terminology rule for ⲥⲃⲱ.

Translated 'her duration' tentatively. ϭⲁⲧ etymology unclear; possibly relates to a Lyc. duration/extent root, or could be a hapax meaning 'flooding/swelling' fitting the Tigris-flood narrative that follows. The doubled ⲧⲉ ⲧⲉ may be scribal dittography. Confidence low; flagged for parallels.

Preserved as 'Concerning' in parentheses. The recurring ⲍ̄ⲁ markers in lines 21-24 appear to function as marginal/rubric repetitions of the chapter-heading particle ⲍⲁ/ⲍⲁⲡⲣⲁ 'concerning' (cf. accumulated vocabulary). They frame the kephalaion title without contributing new content.

Translated 'multiplied, rising up.' ⲁϣⲉⲓⲧⲉ likely from ⲁϣⲁⲓ̈ 'be many, multiply' (cf. accumulated vocabulary ⲁϣⲉⲓⲧⲉ 'multitude/abundance'); ⲧⲟⲛⲱ = ⲧⲱⲟⲩⲛ 'rise up' (3pl perfect). Together describe the river's flood-swell rising under the lions.

Translated 'they sprang forth.' Lyc. reflex possibly of ⲡⲱϩⲧ 'pour forth' or ⲡⲱⲣϣ 'spread.' Confidence low; the verbal series ⲃⲱⲍⲧ̄/ⲃⲣ̄ⲃⲣ̄/6ⲱⲣⲉ describes a crescendo of multiplication-ebullition-strengthening of the lions.

Translated 'flood.' Possibly Lyc. variant of ⲏⲙⲏⲣⲉ/ⲙⲣⲱ 'flood, inundation, riverbank.' Context (Tigris in Pharmouthi/April flood season) supports flood-reading; the lions are pushed out by the great inundation.
